```{r}
#| label: setup

          theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank()))

B = bridge$summary
S = opal_c$summary

model_col = c("SS3 B7" = "grey20", O0 = "#7D3C98", O1 = "#2471A3", O2 = "#E59866",

```

# Overview

The 2023 ISC benchmark assessment of North Pacific swordfish (*Xiphias
gladius*) [@isc2023swo] uses Stock Synthesis [SS3 3.30.20; @methot2013]. The
model has two sexes, which differ in growth and natural mortality, and four
seasons (quarters) per year with annual ages. Spawning is in the second
quarter (month 5), recruits settle in month 7, and catch, indices and length
compositions are entered by quarter. Two fleets have blocks of time-varying
selectivity, and one index measures recruitment directly. opal has one sex.
Its SS3 converter handles one season per year. Within a year, opal removes
catch at the start of each season, and it has no recruitment index. The base
case therefore cannot be converted directly.

This case study bridges in two stages:

1. **Within SS3** (@sec-bridge), from the base case to a single-sex, annual
   SS3 model (B7) whose structure opal can represent. Each step makes one
   change, so its effect is measured on its own.
2. **SS3 to opal** (@sec-conversion), converting B7 with the shared converter
   in `shared/ss3-to-opal/`. The conversion is checked and SS3's dynamics are
   replayed with opal's catch timing (@sec-o0). opal is then fitted
   (@sec-fits).

@sec-limitations lists where opal falls short of SS3 or differs from it,
and what opal would need to model the base case itself. The case study
documents these differences; it does not change opal.

```{r}
#| label: headline
b0 = b("00-base"); b1 = b("01-single-sex"); b1s = b("01s-sex-averaged")
b2 = b("02-block-split"); b3 = b("03-spawn-month-1"); b4 = b("04-annual")
b5 = b("05-annual-comps"); b6 = b("06-settle-month-1"); b7 = b("07-index-month-1")
tm = opal_c$timing
tm_end = tm[, .(end = rel[.N], max = max(abs(rel))), by = .(removal, weight)]
br = opal_c$bridge
```

In brief:

* The base case re-runs exactly with SS3 3.30.22.1 (NLL `r fmt(b0$nll, 4)`,
  SSB~2021~ `r fmt(b0$ssb_2021, 0)` t, SSB~MSY~ `r fmt(b0$ssb_msy, 0)` t, as
  in the report's Table S2).
* **Single sex (B1)** is the largest change in the bridge. It applies
  female growth and female M to all fish. Females are larger and, at older
  ages, have much lower M than males (0.22 against 0.36). SSB~0~ falls from
  `r fmt(b0$ssb0, 0)` t to `r fmt(b1$ssb0, 0)` t, and terminal depletion
  from `r fmt(b0$depletion, 3)` to `r fmt(b1$depletion, 3)`. With
  sex-averaged M and growth instead (sensitivity B1s), depletion is
  `r fmt(b1s$depletion, 3)`, close to the base case.
* **The other steps** each move terminal depletion by at most
  `r fmt(max(abs(diff(B[!step %in% c("00-base", "01s-sex-averaged")]$depletion))), 3)`.
  The blocks become fleets exactly. Merging the quarters requires spawning
  at the start of the year, and the B7 model has depletion
  `r fmt(b7$depletion, 3)`.
* **The conversion of B7 is exact** where opal and SS3 share structure. This
  covers catch, indices, compositions, biology, the unfished equilibrium
  and selectivity-at-length. Replaying SS3's numbers-at-age with SS3's catch
  equation and catch weights reproduces SS3's spawning biomass to
  `r sci(tm_end[grepl("Baranov", removal) & weight == "SS3 fleet catch weight"]$max)`.
* **opal at SS3's values (O0)** differs from SS3 through catch timing (up to
  `r pct(tm_end[weight == "start of year (opal)"]$max)` in spawning biomass
  from removing the year's catch at its start) and through its initial
  equilibrium (`r pct(br$rel_opal[1], 1)` in 1975).
* **opal fitted with SS3's selectivity (O1)** converges and estimates
  terminal depletion `r fmt(o("O1")$depletion_2021, 3)` (SS3 B7:
  `r fmt(o("SS3 B7")$depletion_2021, 3)`). opal's own selectivity curves,
  started at SS3's, are fitted in O2. Eight of their parameters end on a
  bound or cannot be determined. Fixed at their O2 values (O2b), the fit
  converges with the same objective and estimates depletion
  `r fmt(o("O2b")$depletion_2021, 3)`.

# The 2023 assessment {#sec-assessment}

## Stock, fisheries and data

The stock area is the North Pacific north of the equator in the WCPFC
Convention Area and north of 10°N in the IATTC Convention Area. The model
has one area and models the western-central and eastern North Pacific with
fleets as areas. It runs from 1975 to 2021 with four quarterly seasons per
year. Ages are annual (0-15, plus group at 15), with 5 cm population length
bins from 10 to 260 cm.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fleets
#| tbl-cap: "Fleets of the base case and of B7 as opal fisheries. Units: catch (or index) in tonnes (1) or numbers (2). Compositions: fitted length compositions (lambda 0.5 in SS3)."
fl = copy(opal_c$fleets)
knitr::kable(fl[, .(`opal fishery` = fishery, `SS3 fleet` = ss3_fleet, Name = name,
                    Units = units, Compositions = ifelse(lf, "yes", ""))],
             format = "pipe")
```

The base case has 19 fishing fleets. Japanese and US longline catches are
in thousands of fish and all others in tonnes. It has eight abundance
indices, of which S5 (Chinese Taipei longline) and S8 (US shallow-set
longline, late period) have lambda 0. S6, the US deep-set longline index,
is a **recruitment index**: SS3 compares it with the year's age-0
recruitment (units code 33), so its selectivity plays no part. Length
compositions (sex-combined) are entered by quarter. Those of eight fleets
are fitted with lambda 0.5. F5's have lambda 0, and every F9 observation is
excluded (negative year).

## Biology and structure

```{r}
#| label: tbl-structure
#| tbl-cap: "Structure of the base case, from the model files."
knitr::kable(data.table(
    Item = c("SS3 version", "Sexes", "Seasons", "Ages", "Growth", "Natural mortality",
             "Maturity and fecundity", "Spawning and settlement",
             "Stock-recruitment", "Recruitment deviations", "Fishing mortality",
             "Selectivity", "Initial equilibrium", "Catchability", "Data weighting"),
    `Base case` = c(
        "3.30.20.00",
        "2; sex ratio at birth 1:1; SSB is female spawning biomass",
        "4 quarters, 2 subseasons",
        "0-15 (annual)",
        "von Bertalanffy, L1 at age 0.5, L2 at age 15; females 80.1 / 226.3 cm, K 0.246; males 83.4 / 206.4 cm, K 0.271; CV 0.1 (fixed)",
        "age-specific, fixed; females 0.42 at age 0 to 0.22 from age 4; males 0.40 to 0.36",
        "length logistic (L50 143.7 cm); fecundity = weight",
        "spawning month 5 (quarter 2); settlement month 7 at age 0",
        "Beverton-Holt, h = 0.9, sigma_R = 0.42 (fixed)",
        "early 1965-1984, main 1985-2021, bias ramp",
        "hybrid (F method 3); F-ballpark off",
        "length-based double normal (F1, F3, F6, F7, F8) or logistic (F2, F4); other fleets mirror; blocks on F1 (1994-97) and F2 (2004-09)",
        "initial F for F6 (initial-catch lambda 0)",
        "floated q for every index",
        "length compositions lambda 0.5; S5, S8 and F5 compositions lambda 0")),
    format = "pipe")
```

The sexes share selectivity (no sex offsets), weight-length and maturity, and
the compositions are sex-combined. The two sexes therefore differ only in
growth and M. Males are smaller (L2 206.4 against 226.3 cm). From age 4,
males have M of 0.36, against 0.22 for females. The report notes that the
lack of sex-specific size data is one of the two main sources of uncertainty
in the assessment. Section 2.6 of the report describes the model as single
sex, but the model files have two sexes.

# The SS3 bridge {#sec-bridge}

`scripts/01-build-ss3-bridge.r` builds each step and estimates it with SS3
3.30.22.1, Hessian included. Each step makes one change:

* **B0**: as supplied, re-run with 3.30.22.1 from the supplied par file.
* **B1**: single sex (`Nsexes = -1`, so spawning biomass is that of the
  single sex times the female fraction 0.5). Female growth, M and
  weight-length are used, and the sex-combined compositions keep one copy of
  their vector.
* **B1s** (sensitivity, built from B0): as B1, with sex-averaged biology. M
  at age is the rate that takes the unfished numbers of both sexes from one
  age to the next. L1, L2 and K are fitted to the mean length-at-age of the
  two sexes, weighted by their unfished numbers.
* **B2**: the selectivity blocks become fleets, together with every fleet
  that mirrors a blocked fleet. The 1994-97 fleets are F1, F12 and the index
  S2 (fleets 28-30). The 2004-09 fleets are F2, F15, F16 and F19 (fleets
  31-34). F13 and F14 mirror F2 and F1 but have no catch in the block years.
  S5 has lambda 0 and is not split.
* **B3**: spawning in month 1 (season 1) instead of month 5.
* **B4**: one season, with the catches summed over the quarters.
* **B5**: one length composition per fleet and year, combining the quarters
  (sample sizes summed, proportions weighted by sample size).
* **B6**: recruits settle in month 1 at age 0 instead of month 7.
* **B7**: indices observed in month 1.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-bridge
#| tbl-cap: "The SS3 bridge. NLL is SS3's total; B5 changes its constant (see text). F2021 is the average F over ages 1-10. All steps converged (maximum gradient below 2e-3) with a positive-definite Hessian."
stopifnot(all(B$hessian_ok))
knitr::kable(B[, .(Step = label, `Est. par.` = n_par, NLL = fmt(nll, 2),
                   `Max. grad.` = sci(max_gradient), SSB0 = fmt(ssb0, 0),
                   SSB2021 = fmt(ssb_2021, 0), `SSB2021/SSB0` = fmt(depletion, 3),
                   F2021 = fmt(f_2021, 3), `SSB MSY` = fmt(ssb_msy, 0))],
             format = "pipe", align = "lrrrrrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-bridge
#| fig-height: 6.5
#| fig-cap: "Female spawning biomass (top) and depletion (bottom) along the SS3 bridge. B5 and B7 coincide with B4 and B6."
ts = copy(bridge$timeseries)[!step %in% c("05-annual-comps", "07-index-month-1")]
ts[, label := factor(label, levels = bridge$labels)]
long = melt(ts[, .(label, year, `Spawning biomass (t)` = ssb, `SSB / SSB0` = depletion)],
            id.vars = c("label", "year"))
ggplot(long, aes(year, value, colour = label, linetype = label == "B1s sex-averaged biology")) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.7) +
    facet_wrap(~variable, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_linetype_manual(values = c(`FALSE` = "solid", `TRUE` = "22"), guide = "none") +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

**Single sex (B1).** This step changes the stock most. The compositions are
sex-combined, so no data are lost and the length NLL changes little
(`r fmt(b0$nll_length, 1)` to `r fmt(b1$nll_length, 1)`). The population
dynamics change, however. Applied to every fish, the female M of 0.22 from
age 4 gives males a much longer life than their own M of 0.36. Female growth
also makes the males larger. SSB~0~ falls from `r fmt(b0$ssb0, 0)` t to
`r fmt(b1$ssb0, 0)` t and terminal depletion from `r fmt(b0$depletion, 3)` to
`r fmt(b1$depletion, 3)`. The initial F of F6 rises from
`r fmt(b0$init_f, 2)` to `r fmt(b1$init_f, 2)`, so the 1975 stock starts
further down. B1s, with M and growth averaged over the sexes, gives SSB~0~
`r fmt(b1s$ssb0, 0)` t, depletion `r fmt(b1s$depletion, 3)` and initial F
`r fmt(b1s$init_f, 2)`. Its NLL (`r fmt(b1s$nll, 2)`) is lower than B1's.
The difference between B1 and B1s is the cost of choosing one sex's biology
for both. In B1s, F4's logistic inflection lies within SS3's status margin
of its upper bound of 150 cm (148.8 cm; the base case's is 148.3 cm).

**Blocks as fleets (B2).** At B1's estimates B2 reproduces B1's likelihood
components exactly (checked by evaluating B2 at B1's parameters). The only
change is S2's catchability: S2 in 1994-97 is an index of its own with its
own floated q. SS3's q mirror (link type 2) would share S2's q. That version
reproduces B1 at B1's estimates, but the gradient of the shared q is wrong
there (4.3 at B1's optimum), and the minimiser stops short with gradients of
5-60. With its own q, B2 converges at NLL `r fmt(b2$nll, 3)`
(B1: `r fmt(b1$nll, 3)`). The stock barely moves (depletion
`r fmt(b2$depletion, 3)`).

**Timing and seasons (B3-B7).** SS3 does not allow spawning after the start
of the season in which recruits settle. A one-season model with settlement
in month 7 therefore needs spawning at the start of the year, which B3
introduces while the model is still quarterly. Spawning in month 1 rather
than 5 removes four months of mortality before spawning. SSB~0~ rises to
`r fmt(b3$ssb0, 0)` t and depletion to `r fmt(b3$depletion, 3)`. Merging the
quarters (B4) changes the timing of the catch, which is now removed through
the year rather than quarter by quarter. It also changes the fishery
compositions' expected lengths, which become catch-weighted over the year.
Depletion moves to `r fmt(b4$depletion, 3)`, but the initial F falls from
`r fmt(b3$init_f, 2)` to `r fmt(b4$init_f, 2)`: in an annual model the
initial equilibrium needs a much smaller F to give the same 1975 stock.
Combining the quarterly compositions (B5) leaves every estimate unchanged.
Within a year they share one expected composition, so the multinomial kernel
is unchanged. SS3's NLL falls from `r fmt(b4$nll, 1)` to `r fmt(b5$nll, 1)`
only because its composition likelihood includes the observed proportions'
own entropy, which differs between quarterly and annual vectors. Settlement
at the start of the year (B6) makes age-0 fish a full year old at the end of
the year, as in opal. Depletion moves to `r fmt(b6$depletion, 3)` and F~MSY~
from `r fmt(b5$f_msy, 3)` to `r fmt(b6$f_msy, 3)`. Observing the indices in
month 1 (B7) changes nothing for the fitted indices. With two subseasons,
SS3 places observations in months 1-6 at the same time, and the indices
moved are observed in months 1 or 4 (S6, a recruitment index, does not
depend on timing). Only S5, with lambda 0, moves from month 7.

**Starting values.** The control file's INIT values are the supplied
estimates, but the recruitment deviations in the control file start at
zero. Estimated from the control file, the base case converges to a worse
minimum (NLL 332.18 against 289.30). Each step therefore starts from the
previous step's par file where the parameter layout allows (B2-B7). B1 and
B1s start from the control file plus the previous step's deviations, read
through the control file's `read_recdevs` option. Each step is then re-run
from its own par file until its maximum gradient is below 1e-3, because the
control file's INIT values are rounded to six digits. B4 starts from B3's
estimates with the initial F at 0.6 and ln(R~0~) raised by 0.5. From B3's
initial F of 1.59 the annual model's initial stock is a few percent of
SSB~0~ and cannot support the catch.

# Converting B7 to opal {#sec-conversion}

`scripts/02-convert-fit-npo-swo-opal.r` converts B7 with
`config/npo-swo-b7.yaml`. opal has 47 annual time steps of one season and
ages 0-15. Recruits enter at age 0 at the start of the year from that year's
spawning biomass, as in B7. The 25 fishing fleets become opal fisheries 1-25
in SS3 order, and the seven indices with lambda 1 become fisheries 26-32.
The biology (weight, maturity, spawning output and M at age) is SS3's
start-of-year endgrowth table. Spawning output is mature female biomass
times the female fraction 0.5.

## Reconciliation

```{r}
#| label: tbl-recon
#| tbl-cap: "Reconciliation with SS3 (exact comparisons). The 25 catch totals are summarised in one row."
rc = copy(opal_c$recon)
catch_rows = grepl("^catch total", rc$quantity)
rc_tab = rbind(
    data.table(quantity = sprintf("catch totals, %d fleets", sum(catch_rows)),
               rel_diff = max(abs(rc$rel_diff[catch_rows])), pass = all(rc$pass[catch_rows])),
    rc[!catch_rows & !is.na(pass), .(quantity, rel_diff = abs(rel_diff), pass)])
knitr::kable(rc_tab[, .(Quantity = quantity, `Max. rel. diff.` = sci(rel_diff), Pass = pass)],
             format = "pipe")
```

## Growth and length-at-age

opal's growth curve does not enter the biology on this route. It only maps
length-based selectivity to age and predicts the length compositions
through opal's probability of length at age. SS3 builds a fishery's
selectivity-at-age and its expected compositions from mid-year lengths,
because the fishery's catch is taken through the year. opal's growth is
therefore fitted to SS3's mid-year length-at-age. The start-of-year lengths
cannot be fitted in any case. SS3 grows age-0 fish linearly from 10 cm at
settlement to L1 at age 0.5. A Schnute curve through them misses by up to
`r fmt(opal_c$growth_fit_beg$max_abs_error, 0)` cm (RMSE
`r fmt(opal_c$growth_fit_beg$rmse, 1)` cm). At mid-year, the RMSE is
`r fmt(opal_c$growth_fit$rmse, 2)` cm (@fig-laa).

```{r}
#| label: fig-laa
#| fig-height: 3.5
#| fig-cap: "Length-at-age: SS3 B7 at the start of the year and at mid-year, opal's Schnute curve fitted to each (the mid-year fit is used)."
laa = melt(opal_c$laa, id.vars = "age")
laa[, variable := factor(variable, levels = c("ss3_beg", "opal_beg_fit", "ss3_mid", "opal"),
                         labels = c("SS3 start of year", "opal fit to start of year",
                                    "SS3 mid-year", "opal fit to mid-year (used)"))]
ggplot(laa, aes(age, value, colour = variable, shape = variable)) +
    geom_line() + geom_point() +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("grey40", "#E59866", "black", "#2471A3")) +
    labs(x = "Age", y = "Length (cm)", colour = NULL, shape = NULL) +
    guides(colour = guide_legend(nrow = 2))
```

## Selectivity and the recruitment index

opal's double normal and logistic curves reproduce SS3's
selectivity-at-length for every fishery to within
`r sci(max(opal_c$seed_check[fishery != fishery[name == "S6_US_WCNPO_LL_deep"]]$max_abs_diff))`.
The fleets that mirror another take their source fleet's parameters. Mapped
to age through opal's growth, the starting selectivity-at-age is within
`r fmt(max(opal_c$sel_start_diff$max_abs_diff), 3)` of SS3's for every
fishery.

S6 has no opal equivalent. opal predicts an index from numbers- or
biomass-at-age times a selectivity. S6 is therefore converted as an index in
numbers whose selectivity is 1 at age 0 and 0 at older ages. Its observation
at the start of year *y* then predicts that year's age-0 recruits, as SS3's
does. In O0 and O1 this is a row of SS3's selectivity-at-age.
`sel_fa_external` replaces the selectivity of every fishery, so in O2 (opal's
own curves) S6 is an age-based (`sel_basis_f = 2`) double normal. Its peak
is at age -1, so the plateau, which is at least one age wide, ends at age 0,
and both limbs are steep. It gives selectivity 1 at age 0 and below 1e-4 at
older ages, and is fixed. The converter reads SS3's units code 33 as biomass
and S6's size pattern 0 as selectivity 1 at every age. The script overrides
both.

# opal at SS3's values {#sec-o0}

O0 is opal at B7's parameter values with SS3's selectivity-at-age, and
nothing estimated.

```{r}
#| label: fig-o0
#| fig-height: 5.5
#| fig-cap: "O0 against SS3 B7: spawning biomass (top) and relative difference (bottom). The replays start from SS3's 1975 numbers-at-age with SS3's recruitment each year and differ only in how the catch is removed."
tl = copy(tm)[, .(year, series = paste0(removal, "; ", weight), ssb, rel)]
o0 = data.table(year = 1975:2021, series = "O0 (opal)", ssb = br$opal, rel = br$rel_opal)
ss = data.table(year = 1975:2021, series = "SS3 B7", ssb = br$ss3, rel = 0)
d = rbind(ss, o0, tl[grepl("opal|Baranov, SS3\\); SS3", series)])
p1 = ggplot(d, aes(year, ssb, colour = series)) + geom_line() +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Spawning biomass (t)", colour = NULL)
p2 = ggplot(d, aes(year, rel, colour = series)) + geom_line() +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = "grey50") +
    scale_y_continuous(labels = scales::percent) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Relative to SS3", colour = NULL)
(p1 / p2) + plot_layout(guides = "collect") & theme(legend.position = "bottom") &
    guides(colour = guide_legend(ncol = 2))
```

Two things separate O0 from SS3.

**The initial equilibrium.** SS3 solves the 1975 equilibrium with F6's
initial F applied through the year. opal removes the equilibrium catch at
the start of the year. opal's 1975 numbers-at-age are
`r pct(opal_c$init_numbers$rel[1], 1)` above SS3's at age 0, rising to
`r pct(max(opal_c$init_numbers$rel), 0)` in the plus group, and its 1975
spawning biomass is `r pct(br$rel_opal[1], 1)` above SS3's.

**Catch timing and catch weight.** @tbl-timing replays SS3's dynamics (SS3's
1975 numbers and SS3's recruits) with each year's catch removed in
different ways. Removing it through the year (Baranov, as SS3's hybrid F),
with each fleet's SS3 catch weight-at-age, reproduces SS3 to
`r sci(tm_end[grepl("Baranov", removal) & weight == "SS3 fleet catch weight"]$max)`.
This confirms that the converted catch, selectivity, M, spawning output and
units are SS3's. Removing the catch at the start of the year, as opal does,
leaves spawning biomass up to
`r pct(tm_end[weight == "start of year (opal)"]$max)` above SS3's. The
start-of-year weights opal uses partly offset this. With SS3's (larger)
catch weights, a start-of-year removal takes fewer fish of the
weight-based fleets, and the difference grows to
`r pct(tm_end[grepl("opal", removal) & weight == "SS3 fleet catch weight"]$max)`.
A mid-year (Pope) removal is within
`r pct(tm_end[grepl("Pope", removal)]$max)`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-timing
#| tbl-cap: "SS3's dynamics replayed with different catch removals: spawning biomass relative to SS3 B7 in 2021 and the largest absolute difference over 1975-2021."
knitr::kable(tm_end[, .(Removal = removal, `Catch weight` = weight,
                        `2021` = pct(end, 1), `Max.` = pct(max, 1))], format = "pipe")
```

# opal fits {#sec-fits}

Growth, steepness (0.9), sigma~R~ (0.42), M and the biology stay at SS3's
values, as in SS3. opal's default priors are switched off (SS3's prior
lambda is 0) and the length compositions carry SS3's lambda of 0.5. Every
fit estimates B~0~, the recruitment deviations for 1976-2021, the
initial-age deviations of the cohorts born 1965-1975, F6's initial F and the
seven catchabilities. SS3 floats q, and opal estimates it.

* **O1**: SS3's selectivity-at-age, fixed.
* **O2**: opal's selectivity curves, started at SS3's. The parameters SS3
  estimates are estimated (26, with the mirrors sharing their source
  fleet's).
* **O2b**: O2 refitted with the selectivity parameters it cannot determine
  fixed at their O2 values (@tbl-selfixed).
* **O1-noLF**: O1 without the length compositions.
* **O1-noS6**: O1 without the recruitment index (the report's sensitivity
  15).

```{r}
#| label: tbl-fits
#| tbl-cap: "Fits. The objective values are opal's and are not comparable with SS3's likelihood (different constants)."
knitr::kable(S[, .(Model = model, `Est. par.` = n_par,
                   Objective = ifelse(is.na(objective), "", fmt(objective, 2)),
                   `Max. grad.` = ifelse(is.na(max_gradient), "", sci(max_gradient)),
                   `PD Hessian` = ifelse(is.na(positive_hessian), "", positive_hessian),
                   B0 = fmt(B0, 0), `Init. F (F6)` = fmt(init_F6, 3),
                   SSB2021 = fmt(ssb_2021, 0), `SSB2021/B0` = fmt(depletion_2021, 3))],
             format = "pipe", align = "lrrrcrrrr")
```

```{r}
#| label: fits-text
o1 = o("O1"); o2 = o("O2"); o2b = o("O2b"); ss3 = o("SS3 B7")
```

O1 converges with a positive-definite Hessian. It estimates a stock of
similar size (B~0~ `r fmt(o1$B0, 0)` against `r fmt(ss3$B0, 0)` t) that is
less depleted than SS3's (`r fmt(o1$depletion_2021, 3)` against
`r fmt(ss3$depletion_2021, 3)` in 2021). This is in the direction and of
roughly the size of O0's offset, which comes from catch timing and the
initial equilibrium. Without the compositions (O1-noLF) depletion is
`r fmt(o("O1-noLF")$depletion_2021, 3)`. Without S6 (O1-noS6) it is
`r fmt(o("O1-noS6")$depletion_2021, 3)`, so the recruitment index has
little leverage on opal's estimate of the stock's state.

O2 reaches a lower objective than O1 (`r fmt(o2$objective, 1)` against
`r fmt(o1$objective, 1)`), but stops with a gradient of
`r sci(o2$max_gradient)` and a Hessian that is not positive definite. Four
of its selectivity parameters end on SS3's bounds. F2's logistic inflection
(SS3's bound of 150 cm; SS3's own estimate for F4 is also close to its 150
cm bound) is one. The descending widths of F3, F6 and F8 reach SS3's lower
bounds, where the likelihood is flat because their plateaus extend to the
largest length. Fixing these, and then the parameters that dominate the
remaining flat directions of the Hessian (@tbl-selfixed), gives O2b. O2b has
the same objective, converges with a positive-definite Hessian, and
estimates terminal depletion `r fmt(o2b$depletion_2021, 3)`.

```{r}
#| label: tbl-selfixed
#| tbl-cap: "Selectivity parameters fixed in O2b (opal scale), and why: on a bound in O2, or dominating a flat direction of the Hessian (eigenvalue below 1e-6). Columns of the double normal: 1 peak, 2 top, 3 ascending width, 4 descending width; of the logistic: 1 inflection, 2 width."
knitr::kable(opal_c$sel_fixed[, .(Fishery = fishery, Name = name, Column = column,
                                  Value = fmt(value, 2), Reason = reason)], format = "pipe")
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-fits
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Spawning biomass, depletion and age-0 recruitment: SS3 B7 and the opal models (O2, not converged, is not shown; O2b has the same estimates)."
tr = copy(opal_c$trajectory)[model != "O2"]
tr[, model := factor(model, levels = names(model_col))]
long = melt(tr, id.vars = c("model", "year"),
            measure.vars = c("ssb", "depletion", "recruits"))
long[, variable := factor(variable, labels = c("Spawning biomass (t)", "SSB / B0",
                                               "Age-0 recruits (1000s)"))]
ggplot(long, aes(year, value, colour = model)) +
    geom_line(linewidth = 0.6) +
    facet_wrap(~variable, ncol = 1, scales = "free_y") +
    scale_colour_manual(values = model_col) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, colour = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-cpue
#| fig-height: 7
#| fig-cap: "Fits to the indices (points: observed, with 95% intervals from the input SE). S6 is the recruitment index; O1-noS6 does not fit it (not shown for S6)."
cp = copy(opal_c$cpue)
cp = merge(cp, opal_c$index_names, by = "index")
cp[, name := sub("_WCNPO", "", name)]
cp = cp[!(model == "O1-noS6" & grepl("^S6", name))]
obs = unique(cp[model == "SS3 B7", .(name, year, obs, se)])
ggplot() +
    geom_pointrange(data = obs, aes(year, obs, ymin = obs * exp(-1.96 * se),
                                    ymax = obs * exp(1.96 * se)), colour = "grey50", size = 0.2) +
    geom_line(data = cp, aes(year, pred, colour = model)) +
    facet_wrap(~name, scales = "free", ncol = 2) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = model_col) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "Index", colour = NULL)
```

```{r}
#| label: fig-sel
#| fig-height: 8
#| fig-cap: "Selectivity-at-age in 2021: SS3 B7 (black) and opal O2b (red), for the fisheries with length compositions and the source fleets of the indices."
sel = copy(opal_c$selectivity)
keep = c(1, 2, 3, 4, 6, 7, 8, 20, 22)
sel = sel[fishery %in% keep]
sel[, name := opal_c$fleets$name[fishery]]
ggplot(sel, aes(age, sel, colour = model)) +
    geom_line() +
    facet_wrap(~name, ncol = 3) +
    scale_colour_manual(values = c("SS3 B7" = "black", O2b = "#C0392B")) +
    labs(x = "Age", y = "Selectivity", colour = NULL)
```

# Limitations and differences from SS3 {#sec-limitations}

## Not available in opal

* **Two sexes.** opal tracks one population vector and scales spawning
  potential by a sex ratio. Modelling the base case needs a sex dimension in
  the numbers-at-age, sex-specific growth and M, and spawning biomass from
  females only. The compositions here are sex-combined, so sex-specific
  composition likelihoods are not needed. The predicted combined composition
  would sum the two sexes' catches. B1 against B1s and B0 shows that the
  choice of single-sex biology moves terminal depletion between
  `r fmt(b1$depletion, 3)` (female) and `r fmt(b1s$depletion, 3)`
  (sex-averaged), against `r fmt(b0$depletion, 3)` with two sexes.
* **Seasons with annual ages.** opal has `n_season`, and within a season its
  catch and index predictions are seasonal. However:
  - it predicts compositions from the year's total catch-at-age with one
    length-at-age for the whole year, not by season;
  - it has one weight-at-age vector for the year;
  - it spawns and recruits only at the start of season 1, whereas the base
    case spawns in month 5 and recruits settle in month 7.

  The SS3-to-opal converter handles one season per year only. Seasonal opal
  models would also need season-specific length-at-age (growth evaluated at
  the season's midpoint) to predict quarterly compositions.
* **Spawning and settlement timing.** opal's spawning biomass is that at the
  start of the year, before any mortality. B3 shows that moving spawning
  from month 5 to month 1 raises SSB~0~ by
  `r pct(b3$ssb0 / b2$ssb0 - 1)` and terminal depletion from
  `r fmt(b2$depletion, 3)` to `r fmt(b3$depletion, 3)`. A spawning-time
  fraction (M and F applied before spawning) would remove this step.
* **Time-varying selectivity.** Blocks cannot be estimated. Blocks that
  replace parameters are reproduced exactly by splitting the fleet (B2), but
  every fleet that mirrors a blocked fleet has to be split too (here seven
  fleets). A split index needs its own catchability or a shared one, and
  SS3's shared q (link 2) does not converge.
* **Recruitment index.** opal has no index of the year's recruitment (SS3
  units 33). An index in numbers with age-0 selectivity reproduces it at the
  start of the year. Because `sel_fa_external` replaces every fishery's
  selectivity, a fit with opal's own curves needs an age-based curve pinned
  to that shape. A per-fishery external selectivity, or an index type for
  recruitment (or for any age range), would avoid the workaround.
* **Analytical (floated) catchability.** SS3 solves q; opal estimates it.

## Structural differences handled in the conversion

* **Catch timing.** opal removes each season's catch at its start; SS3's
  hybrid F removes it through the season. At SS3's values this leaves
  spawning biomass up to `r pct(tm_end[weight == "start of year (opal)"]$max)`
  above SS3's (@tbl-timing). A mid-season (Pope) removal would be within
  `r pct(tm_end[grepl("Pope", removal)]$max)`. Quarterly opal seasons would
  also approximate SS3's removal.
* **Initial equilibrium.** opal's initial equilibrium removes the initial-F
  catch at the start of the year. Its 1975 spawning biomass at SS3's values
  is `r pct(br$rel_opal[1], 1)` above SS3's. A Baranov or mid-year removal in
  `get_initial_numbers()` would match SS3.
* **Catch weight.** opal converts catch in weight to numbers with one
  weight-at-age (start of year here). SS3 uses each fleet's catch
  weight-at-age (selectivity-weighted, mid-season).
* **Length-at-age for selectivity and compositions.** SS3 forms a fishery's
  selectivity-at-age and expected compositions from mid-year lengths. opal
  uses one length-at-age, here fitted to SS3's mid-year lengths. The
  biology stays at the start of the year.
* **Growth below the first reference age.** SS3 grows age-0 fish linearly
  from settlement to L1 at age 0.5. opal's Schnute curve cannot represent
  this, which matters only at the start of the year.
* **Fleet layout.** SS3 3.30 allows fishing fleets after the surveys (here
  the block fleets 28-34). The converter maps SS3 fleets to opal fisheries
  by fleet type.

## What the bridge itself changes

The single-sex step is not neutral. B1 applies female M and growth to
every fish. Males live longer and grow larger than they do in the base case,
and the stock is smaller and more depleted. B1s, with sex-averaged biology,
is closer to the base case. Either choice is an approximation that opal's
lack of sexes forces. With the sex-combined compositions here, a two-sex
opal would need no new data. The timing steps (B3, B6) move spawning and
settlement to the start of the year. B3 is required for SS3 itself to merge
the seasons, and both change the stock's scale and productivity
(SSB~MSY~, F~MSY~). These are differences between the base case and opal's
structure, not between SS3 and opal.

# Reproducing this document {.unnumbered}

| Step | Script | Writes |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `scripts/01-build-ss3-bridge.r` | the SS3 bridge models and `vignettes/data/npo-swo-ss3-bridge-cache.rds` |
| 2 | `scripts/02-convert-fit-npo-swo-opal.r` | `vignettes/data/npo-swo-opal-cache.rds` and the fitted models |
| 3 | `quarto render vignettes/npo-swo-ss3-to-opal.qmd` | this document |

```{r}
#| label: session
cat(sprintf("Caches: bridge %s (SS3 %s); opal %s (opal %s, r4ss %s, R %s).\n",
            bridge$made_at, bridge$ss3_version, opal_c$created,
            opal_c$session$opal, opal_c$session$r4ss, opal_c$session$r))
```
